title: Graceful Arabic Paisley Mehndi Design for Arm
descriptionParagraphs: An elegant arabic mehndi design tailored for the arm, featuring diamond lattice and bell garland. Rated as Expert, this pattern is perfect for a party.

Henna on the forearm stains lighter than on the palm because the skin is thinner. Arm designs are easier to apply on someone else than on yourself, especially past the wrist. This is a detailed pattern usually done by an experienced artist; allow plenty of time and work in small sections.

The negative space in Arabic henna is intentional — it allows each motif to stand out dramatically. In Emirati tradition, henna is applied to both hands and feet of the bride by a professional 'hannaya'.

image.alt: Arabic Paisley mehndi design for arm — graceful henna pattern

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

faq.q: How can I make my mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave the paste on longer, seal it with lemon and sugar, keep the skin warm, and avoid water for the first day after removing the paste.
